items.title: Larry Gold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2025
items.q: The interviewee discusses attending 'Curtis' (Curtis Institute of Music) as an institution and mentions 'Curtis background' and 'violinists at Curtis', but does not mention a specific person named Curtis.

ctx.x: Did you find that — this is an observation again but playing the cello and then being at Curtis in ensembles, I'm guessing it must have paid off really well when you started arranging and composing, not only for the strings but just observing brass players and knowing what's capable, what's going to make them sound the best where to breathe etcetera.

You know I'm going to give you a little secret here. I was part of that Philly Sound. And what I did originally when I was little — when I was little — in my 20s I learned how these great older arrangers wrote for the MFSB which was the orchestra in Philadelphia at that time. So a lot of my initial stuff was not only my Curtis background but it was sitting there playing and listening to what they had done for the last eight years or so. And so yes it became second—hand, it became really easy for me to write…
Some of that is not answerable. That's what I think makes it so wonderful is that you can't pin down why things work or why some particular record that you might not even anticipate becomes a hit.
